Billy Corgan made an inciteful comment about MTV recently. Basically, MTV became popular by paying licensing fees to play the intellectual property of others (all the music videos we loved to watch). In between blocks of videos they would play their own music related shows to support the music videos, but their programming was always secondary and supported the music videos/culture.

Once MTV's market saturation became more or less a monopoly they began churning out original TV programming to avoid paying licensing fees on music videos. The programming they created was "reality" oriented (weak or no script) and typically featured no name or B list actors. The goal was to increase profitability for a given block of programming by decreasing costs without losing viewership. Fortunately for them, the mindless youth ate it up and the transition was drawn out enough, so they got away with it.

TL;DR MTV used the intellectual property of artists to gain popularity then abandoned their music and videos over time in favor of less costly in-house programming.
